summary: Invoice shows separate 'cache-hit tokens' line plus 'generated tokens' for same time window — clarification and potential adjustment requested
description: BoltAI reports that their February invoice (INV-2026-02-987) contains two distinct line items for the same API key/time window: one labeled 'generated tokens' and another labeled 'cache-hit tokens (KV prefix hits)'. They expected only generated token billing and to see cache hits reflected only in latency/cost dashboards, not as separate billable lines. BoltAI is a dedicated customer with a reserved pool; they suspect double-counting or a new meter introduced during a recent metering change. They provided a CSV extract and a billing JSON snippet. Customer requests: 1) explanation of why cache-hit tokens appear separately, 2) confirmation whether cache hits are billable, 3) if this is an error, request for credit for the February invoice, and 4) recommendations to avoid surprises going forward.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's production API key to run a standard chat generation workload that leverages prefix caching (KV cache enabled in deployment config).
2) Run a 3-day batch of repeated prompt variants that should hit the cache ~65% of the time, and record tokens generated vs. returned from cache in the runtime metrics console.
3) Download billing invoice CSV for the same window and inspect lines for that API key. Note presence of both 'generated' and 'cache-hit' lines with overlapping timestamps.
4) Compare runtime token counters (runtime/tracing) to invoice meter rows for token counts and prices per token.
5) Share artifacts: runtime metrics links, raw CSV, and the invoice PDF.
observed_behavior: Invoice shows two line items for the same hour ranges: one with 1,245,320 generated tokens and a second labeled 'cache-hit tokens' with 812,450 tokens. The customer sees in the runtime console that ~810k tokens were served from KV cache and expected these to be excluded from billable generated token usage or be discounted under their dedicated contract. The invoice's unit price for 'cache-hit tokens' matches the standard per-token generation price, producing a ~40% higher charge than expected.
expected_behavior: Customer expected billing to only show 'generated tokens' (tokens actually produced by the model) and for cache hits to either be unbilled or billed at a clearly documented reduced rate per the dedicated contract. At minimum, they expected the billing UI to explain why cache-hit tokens are appearing as a separate charged meter.

investigation_notes: Reviewed change log for metering pipeline: PR #1898 added a distinct meter for kv cache hits to enable more granular telemetry and cost attribution for hosted customers.
Dedicated pricing contract language: does not list cache-hit tokens as a separate billable meter; billing system should map cache hits into net generated token accounting for dedicated customers.
Metering pipeline bug: new job emits cache_hit_tokens_v2 independently rather than subtracting hits from generated_tokens for customers with 'dedicated' pricing flag.

Preliminary impact: for this customer the duplicate meter resulted in double-billing for tokens that should have been counted as cache hits only (i.e., should have reduced generated token count). Estimated overcharge for February: $2,150 before any volume discounts.
Scope: quick scan indicates other dedicated customers with KV caching enabled may be impacted for dates 2026-02-08 through 2026-02-28. Full list pending audit (INT-4021).
Risk: hosted/self-serve customers were intended to be billed separately for cache hits; change mistakenly affected dedicated flag path.
Next action: billing to create provisional credit and follow with final audit and postmortem. Engineering to deploy suppression patch to metering job and add contract-aware mapping tests.
resolution: Provisional credit issued for BoltAI's February invoice equal to the duplicate 'cache_hit_tokens_v2' charges (credit reference CR-2026-03-045). Billing team will finalize audit and post final adjustment by 2026-03-07. Engineering patched metering job to respect 'dedicated' contract flag (INT-4021) and added unit/integration tests to prevent reintroduction. Customer asked to confirm when they receive the credit; support to close after confirmation. Follow-up: confluence doc updated to explain cache-hit billing semantics and dedicated customer mapping.
